answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks by requiring verifiable energy-burn proofs for node registration. Each agent must submit cryptographic meter signatures showing dedicated electrical draw—such as from shale gas or municipal grids—fed through copper wiring. The consensus kernel validates this expenditure before granting credentials, imposing a scarce kilowatt-hour cost per replica. However, this mechanism encourages environmental waste and disadvantages low-resource participants.
